Question B-007-005-004.

Why the correct answer is right: The solar-flux index is a measured indication of solar activity taken at a defined radio frequency. That fixed-frequency measurement makes readings comparable from day to day.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Another name for the smoothed sunspot number (SSN)": Smoothed sunspot number is based on counted spots averaged over time. It is not the same measurement as radio solar flux.
- sourceIndex 2: "A measure of solar activity that compares daily readings with results from the last six months": A six-month comparison is a trend method, not the definition of the solar-flux index.
- sourceIndex 3: "A measure of solar activity that is taken annually": Solar flux is monitored regularly for current conditions, so an annual-only reading would miss the changes operators care about.
